controls.title: Exterior opening detection
controls.objective: Every exterior door and accessible ground-floor window is covered by an intrusion sensor.

questions.text: Is every exterior door fitted with a contact or covered by a detector that is armed after hours?
questions.guidance: Compare the zone list with doors on site. Partial: some doors covered.

questions.text: Are accessible ground-floor windows and roof hatches covered by contacts, glass-break, or motion detection?
questions.guidance: Accessible means reachable from grade or a climbable feature without a ladder.

references.source: NFPA 731, Installation of Electronic Premises Security Systems

controls.title: Interior detection of high-value areas
controls.objective: High-value interior areas are covered by interior detection independent of perimeter sensors.

evidence.description: Photo of detectors and their coverage

questions.text: Are server rooms, cash rooms, and other high-value rooms covered by an interior detector on a separate zone?
questions.guidance: Check detector placement covers the entry path into the room.

references.source: NFPA 731, Installation of Electronic Premises Security Systems

controls.title: Alarm monitoring and response
controls.objective: Alarms are monitored around the clock by a certified central station or staffed console, with a documented response.

evidence.description: Monitoring contract and central station certificate

questions.text: Is the intrusion system monitored 24 hours a day by a central station with a current UL listing or certificate (or regional equivalent), or by an on-site console staffed at all times?
questions.guidance: Ask for the certificate. Partial: monitored but certificate not available.

questions.text: Measured time from sending a test alarm to operator acknowledgement
questions.guidance: Coordinate a test with the monitoring center. Record the time to acknowledgement and to callback.

questions.text: Is there a written alarm response procedure naming who responds and within what time?
questions.guidance: Partial: response exists but not written.

references.source: UL 2050 and UL 681 (alarm monitoring and installation)

controls.title: Alarm system testing
controls.objective: The intrusion system is tested end to end on a defined schedule and faults are corrected.

questions.text: Months since the last documented end-to-end test of every sensor
questions.guidance: Use the date on the last inspection report. Many standards require at least annual testing; record the number.

questions.text: Number of open faults or troubles shown on the panel or monitoring account
questions.guidance: View the panel and monitoring account history.

references.source: NFPA 731, Installation of Electronic Premises Security Systems

controls.title: Duress and panic alarms
controls.objective: Duress or panic alarms are installed where staff face threats and are tested.

questions.text: Are panic or duress buttons installed at reception and cash-handling positions, and tested in the last 12 months?
questions.guidance: Partial: installed but not tested in 12 months.

references.source: NFPA 731, Installation of Electronic Premises Security Systems

controls.title: Alarm panel protection and communication
controls.objective: The alarm panel is protected against tamper and loss of power or communication, and reports those conditions.

evidence.description: Photo of the panel location and enclosure

questions.text: Is the control panel inside a protected zone, with an enclosure tamper switch and a standby battery?
questions.guidance: Partial: one of the three missing.

questions.text: Does the panel report loss of its primary communication path, using a second path (cellular or network) as backup?
questions.guidance: Ask for the communicator configuration or monitoring account details.

references.source: NFPA 731, Installation of Electronic Premises Security Systems
